evidence.label: Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections

headline: Claimed proofs that curve counts on complete intersections and on projective bundles obey the Virasoro equations.
scope: One paper covers smooth complete intersections in projective space. The other passes the equations from a base to any projective bundle over it.
plain: Gromov–Witten invariants count curves of each shape inside a space. The Virasoro conjecture says that all these counts obey one infinite family of equations. One paper claims this for every smooth complete intersection in projective space, the zero set of several polynomials. A second paper claims the equations pass from a space to any projective bundle built over it. Both cover every genus and every kind of cohomology class.
doesNot: This does not prove the Virasoro conjecture for every smooth projective variety, and nothing here has a Lean check.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Eguchi, Hori and Xiong, who proposed the constraints
scorecard.significanceWhy: It claims the conjecture for a large, standard class of spaces without the semisimplicity hypothesis that earlier all-genus results used.

explanation:
Start with curves mapped to the simplest target, a single point. Fix a genus g, the number of handles of a surface, and n marked points on it. For each point pick a whole number k. These choices give an intersection number on the space of all such curves, written ⟨τ_k1 … τ_kn⟩_g. It can be nonzero only when the k's add up to 3g − 3 + n. Two standard values are ⟨τ_0 τ_0 τ_0⟩_0 = 1 and ⟨τ_1⟩_1 = 1/24.

These numbers obey linear rules. The dilaton rule says that adding a τ_1 multiplies the number by 2g − 2 + n. Here n counts the points before the new one. So ⟨τ_1 τ_0 τ_0 τ_0⟩_0 = (0 − 2 + 3) × 1 = 1. Likewise ⟨τ_1 τ_1⟩_1 = (2 − 2 + 1) × 1/24 = 1/24. The string rule says that adding a τ_0 lowers one other k by one, summed over the choices. So ⟨τ_0 τ_2⟩_1 = ⟨τ_1⟩_1 = 1/24. Witten's conjecture and Kontsevich's theorem fix the whole generating function of these numbers[1]. Its equations include these two rules.

Gromov–Witten invariants make the same kind of count for curves inside a space X. Descendant invariants also record powers of a natural class at each marked point, as k does above. The Virasoro conjecture says their generating function Z obeys equations L_k Z = 0 for every k ≥ −1. The operators L_k depend on X through its pairing of classes, a Hodge grading and its first Chern class[2]. The Hodge grading sorts the cohomology classes of X into types. The first Chern class is a basic curvature class of X.

Eguchi, Hori and Xiong proposed such equations for Fano varieties in 1997[3]. Liu and Tian proved them in genus zero[4]. Givental's methods with Teleman's theorem give all genera when quantum cohomology is generically semisimple[5]. Semisimple roughly means the curve-count multiplication splits into independent one-dimensional pieces. Okounkov and Pandharipande proved the equations for smooth target curves[6]. Coates, Givental and Tseng passed them between a base and toric bundles built from sums of line bundles[7].

The September paper claims the full conjecture for every smooth complete intersection in projective space[8]. A complete intersection is the common zero set of the right number of polynomials, like a smooth cubic surface. The claim covers every genus and curve class. Primitive and odd classes are included, with no semisimplicity hypothesis[9]. The October paper claims a transfer theorem. The equations pass from a base B to the projectivization of any vector bundle of rank at least two[10]. Projectivization replaces each point of B by all lines through the origin of its fiber. The bundle need not split, and it needs no positivity condition[11]. So the result applies again and again to towers of projective bundles[12]. With Okounkov and Pandharipande's theorem, it covers every projective bundle over a smooth curve[13].

The September paper breaks X into simpler pieces glued along a seam, a step called degeneration. Its main obstacle is primitive cohomology. Primitive classes need not extend one at a time through a degeneration[14]. So the paper treats the error in each equation as a single object and probes it with allowed tests[15]. Pairing an error with its complex conjugate, in a second copy of the theory, gives its squared size[16]. That size is positive unless the error is zero, so the error must vanish[17].

How sure is this? There is no Lean scope note for either paper, so no computer proof checker has tested them. Each paper claims its theorem in full, using earlier published results as inputs. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if both papers hold. Neither has a Lean scope note, and both depend on long chains of earlier theorems. No specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A number that counts curves of a given genus and shape inside a space.
A Gromov–Witten count that also records powers of a natural class at each marked point.
An infinite family of linear equations that the generating function of descendant counts is conjectured to obey.
The common zero set of the right number of polynomial equations in projective space.
A space built over a base by replacing each point with all lines through the origin of a vector space.
A property where curve-count multiplication splits into independent one-dimensional pieces.
Breaking a space into simpler pieces glued along a seam, while keeping track of curve counts.

claims.sourceLine: identify the corresponding generating function with the distinguished solution of the KdV hierarchy
claims.sourceQuote: Its simplest instance is the intersection theory of the moduli spaces of curves: Witten's conjecture and Kontsevich's theorem identify the corresponding generating function with the distinguished solution of the KdV hierarchy \cite{Witten1991,Kontsevich1992}.

claims.text: The operators L_k are formed from the Poincaré pairing, the first Hodge index and cup product with c_1(TX).
claims.sourceLine: are formed from the Poincar\'e pairing, the first Hodge index $p$ on $H^{p,q}(X)$, and cup product with $c_1(TX)$
claims.sourceQuote: The conjecture asserts \[ L_k^X Z_X=0\qquad(k\geq-1), \] where the target-dependent differential operators $L_k^X$ are formed from the Poincar\'e pairing, the first Hodge index $p$ on $H^{p,q}(X)$, and cup product with $c_1(TX)$.
